butter.songTitle: Chateau Lobby #4 (in C for Two Virgins)
stanza: Emma eats bread and butter
Like a queen would have ostrich and cobra wine
We'll have Satanic Christmas Eve
And play piano in the Chateau lobby

butter.line: 'Cause overnight that lake had turned as thick as butter
stanza: Some said the local lake had been enchanted
Others said it must have been the weather
The neighbors were trying to keep it quiet
But I swear that I could hear the laughter
So they jokingly nicknamed it the porridge
'Cause overnight that lake had turned as thick as butter
But the local kids would still go swimming, drinking
Saying that to them it doesn't matter

butter.line: It was as if someone had spread butter
butter.linePrev: And circle the blue fields and grease the night
butter.lineNext: On all the fine points of the stars

cutter.line: The beat is so butter, peep the slow cutter
cutter.linePrev: And you know I know that's a bunch of snow
cutter.lineNext: As he utter the calm flow ("Your mother—"), don't talk about my moms, yo

flutter.line: And the money pile on the dashboard fluttering
stanza: It came over her at a bad time
Riding through Winona down the dotted line
Held us gunning out
90 miles down the road of a dead end dream
She looked over with her part smile
Caught up in the twinkle, it could take awhile
And the money pile on the dashboard fluttering

flutter.line: The earth quakes, the sun flakes flutter
stanza: Under the toadstool lover down by the dream
Everything flowing over rainbows downstream
Silver the turning water flying away
I'll come to see you sooner I'm on my way
And there's a mirror that I'm looking straight through
And I get it
And there's a doorway that I'm ducking into
To forget it
But flashing just beyond the sky
The shattering midnight gathers
And reminding me behind my mind
The earth quakes, the sun flakes flutter

gutter.line: I heard the song of a poet who died in the gutter
stanza: And what did you hear, my blue-eyed son?
And what did you hear, my darling young one?
I heard the sound of a thunder that roared out a warning
I heard the roar of a wave that could drown the whole world
I heard one hundred drummers whose hands were a-blazing
I heard ten-thousand whispering and nobody listening
I heard one person starve, I heard many people laughing
I heard the song of a poet who died in the gutter
I heard the sound of a clown who cried in the alley

gutter.songTitle: Now That Your Dollar Bills Have Sprouted Wings
gutter.line: Watching all your coins roll down the gutter
stanza: Watching all your coins roll down the gutter
All your champagne going down the sink
Is there something that you're trying to remember?
Or is that string around your finger a wedding ring?

gutter.line: Or a roach on his way to the gutter
stanza: Thrust into bein', careenin' along
On a crooked little trajectory
Dissolvin' in movement, a body in orbit
Or a roach on his way to the gutter

gutter.line: Because it's made of a hundred gutters
stanza: When I go downtown
I always wear a corduroy suit
Because it's made of a hundred gutters
That the rain can run right through
But a lonely man can't make a move
If he can't even bring himself to choose
Between a pair of black and a pair of brown shoes

gutter.line: From the housetops to the gutters
stanza: From the housetops to the gutters
From the ocean to the shore
The warning signs have all been bright and garish
Far too great in number to ignore
From the cities to the swamplands
From the highways to the hills
Our love has never had a leg to stand on
From the aspirins to the cross-tops to the Elavils

gutter.line: No one ever plans to sleep out in the gutter
stanza: I read the body count out of the paper
And now it’s written all over my face
No one ever plans to sleep out in the gutter
Sometimes that’s just the most comfortable place
